correctness.rationale: For each incidence edge, orientation at the original endpoint converts an induced matching into a partial map with all heads outside its tail set. If either shore of a complete bipartite original is fully selected as tails, every function to the other shore is maximal; otherwise both residual shores are nonempty and all unused tails must be images of opposite-shore functions. Counting surjections gives the exact polynomial. The same argument on a complete original gives a single onto map. Coefficient support follows from positivity of Stirling numbers. The standalone adjacency-based enumeration independently matches all coefficients for 25 graph instances and 51 support checks; finite evidence is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

Yuan et al. (2024) prove connected-graph extremal bounds on counts; Akbari et al. (2019) characterize well-indumatched tree/girth classes. Neither supplies the complete family-specific maximal induced matching polynomial. Matching record searches located no stronger or equivalent all-parameter result. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The full labeled cardinality distribution for every full subdivision of a complete or complete bipartite graph is a natural extremal strong-matching invariant. In I(K_{2,b}), inclusion-maximal induced matchings occur only at sizes 2 and b, so the gap can grow arbitrarily even though the graph is connected and bipartite. The exact Stirling coefficient formulas, support conditions, and top-stratum multiplicities improve materially on merely knowing maximum/minimum cardinalities or enumerating ordinary matchings.
